evidence: src/application/order-service.ts:65 `combineItems` throws DomainError("An order requires at least one item"); the flag reports the same literal at src/domain/order.ts:27 (Order validation).

src/application/order-service.ts:69 `combineItems` checks `!item.productId || !Number.isInteger(item.quantity) || item.quantity <= 0` and throws "Each order item needs a product id and positive integer quantity"; the flag reports the same literal at src/domain/order.ts:30.
src/application/order-service.ts `placeOrder` passes the validated items to `new Order(...)`, so the domain entity's own validation also runs on them. The rule exists twice as a copy.

src/application/catalogue-service.ts and src/application/order-service.ts reach persistence only through the injected ProductRepository and OrderRepository ports. No direct persistence access was found.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The three files form one application-service concern: product catalogue and order use cases plus their DTOs. Both services reach persistence only through the domain repository ports (`ProductRepository` and `OrderRepository`), with no direct database or ORM access. Each service maps to DTOs consistently through its private `toDto`.

The problem is that `OrderService.combineItems` writes out the order-item invariant itself: at least one item, and each item needs a product id and a positive integer quantity. The deterministic flags report the same two error literals at `src/domain/order.ts:27` and `src/domain/order.ts:30`. That indicates the `Order` domain entity already enforces this invariant. `placeOrder` then passes the combined items to `new Order(...)`, so the rule exists twice as a copy rather than as a call to one shared definition. I couldn't see the source of `src/domain/order.ts`, so this depends on the flag locations. The matching exact messages make a copied validation very likely.

Merging duplicate product ids in `combineItems` is a legitimate application-level step and is not a duplicate. The pre-check of stock in `placeOrder` may also repeat a check inside `Product.reserve`. I can't confirm that without `product.ts`, so it is not counted.

violations.message: `OrderService.combineItems` copies the Order item invariant (at least one item; product id and positive integer quantity, with the same error messages) that the domain Order in src/domain/order.ts:27/30 already enforces. The rule is duplicated instead of coming from one shared definition.
